intro: Everything for coaching sales and retention conversations in one place: a call review that turns gaps into coaching, the sales flow with model language, offer guides, objection handling, and buying signals.
notOffer: A payment link, payment arrangement, or other payment assistance helps the customer, but it is not a sales offer. Confirm current offers, eligibility, pricing, and disclosure requirements in approved resources before coaching on them.

steps.title: Understand
steps.good: Let the customer explain the reason for the call without interruption, then restate it in one sentence and confirm it is right.
steps.say: So your bill went up this month and you'd like to understand why. Did I get that right?

steps.title: Empathize
steps.good: Respond to how the situation is affecting the customer, using details they actually shared rather than a general phrase.
steps.say: I'm sorry the internet keeps dropping while you're working from home. That makes the whole workday harder.

steps.title: Assure
steps.good: Tell the customer clearly that you will take care of the concern, and preview the first step.
steps.say: I'm going to take care of this with you today. First, I'll check the connection on your equipment.

steps.title: Probe
steps.good: Ask open questions about the concern, and listen for needs that matter later, such as devices, household, or other providers.
steps.say: When did you first notice it, and is it happening on every device or just one?

steps.title: Resolve
steps.good: Resolve the customer's main concern completely, using the applicable process, before introducing anything else.
steps.say: I found what was causing the drops, and I've reset the connection from our side. Let's make sure it's working for you.

steps.title: Confirm
steps.good: Have the customer confirm the issue is resolved on their side before the conversation moves on.
steps.say: Can you check on your end that everything is loading normally now?

steps.title: Plant the Seed
steps.good: After the resolution is confirmed, mention one relevant idea tied to something the customer shared, with no pressure to decide.
steps.say: You mentioned everyone is online in the evenings. Some households like yours find a faster plan helps with that, and I'm happy to share details whenever it's useful.

steps.title: Relevant Offer
steps.good: Present the offer that matches the need you uncovered and say why you chose it. Payment help does not count as an offer.
steps.say: Based on what you shared about the phone bill with your current carrier, Xfinity Mobile could be worth a look. Would you like me to show you how it could work for your household?

steps.title: Explain Pricing
steps.good: Explain the full price clearly: the promotional price and term, the standard rate afterward, equipment charges, taxes and fees, and any requirements.
steps.say: Here's exactly what you'd pay. The promotional price applies for the promotional term, and then the standard rate applies. Taxes and fees are separate, and your first bill may include a partial month.

steps.title: Confirm Understanding
steps.good: Ask for the decision, then recap what the customer agreed to, what they will pay now and later, and what happens next.
steps.say: Before I place the order, let me recap what you're getting, what you'll pay now and after the promotion, and what happens next. Does that all sound right?

skills.title: Offer value
skills.good: Connect each feature to a benefit tied to the customer's own situation before talking about price.

skills.title: Objection handling
skills.good: Acknowledge the objection, ask one clarifying question, and respond with value tied to that specific concern.

skills.title: Respecting a clear no
skills.good: Accept a clear no the first time, with at most one respectful clarification, and close the call warmly.

skills.title: Buying signals
skills.good: Notice cues such as a price question or a contract ending elsewhere, and follow up with a question.

skills.title: Retention
skills.good: When the customer mentions canceling or switching, ask what is behind it and present the applicable options per the retention process.

offers.title: Xfinity Mobile (XM)
offers.summary: New lines, devices, or moving a number over, for customers whose mobile needs came up in the conversation.
fits: The customer mentions their phone bill or plan with another carrier.
A family member needs a new line, or someone is getting their first phone.
The customer asks about a new device or keeping their current number.
The customer would like fewer separate bills and providers.
questions: Who in your household uses a mobile phone today, and which carrier are you with?
How do you mostly use your phones: calls and texts, streaming, or working on the go?
Are you planning to keep your current phones, or is anyone due for a new device?
offers.seed: Since you mentioned paying a separate phone bill, it may be worth knowing that we also offer mobile service. I'm happy to walk you through it anytime it's useful.
offers.bridge: Now that your internet is working again, can I share one idea about the phone bill you mentioned earlier?
value: Explain how it would work for the lines and devices the customer described, not every feature available.
Connect the benefit to what they told you, such as managing services in one place or keeping their current number.
disclosure: The monthly price for the lines discussed, any promotional term, and the standard rate afterward
Device costs, trade-in conditions, or payment terms, if any
Taxes and fees, and when the first bill arrives
What happens with the current carrier and the number transfer

objection.says: I'm happy with my current carrier.
objection.acknowledge: That's good to hear, and switching isn't something to do without a reason.
objection.clarify: Is there anything about your current plan you'd change if you could, such as the price or the data?
objection.respond: If cost is the main thing, I can show you how the lines you described would compare, and you can decide whether it's worth a closer look.

offers.note: Confirm current Xfinity Mobile offers, eligibility, device programs, and number transfer requirements in approved resources.

offers.title: Service Upgrades
offers.summary: Changes that improve an existing service, such as faster internet or updated equipment, when the household's usage has outgrown the current setup.
fits: Several people stream, game, or work online at the same time.
Evenings or video calls slow down, and troubleshooting confirms the service itself is working as designed.
Wi-Fi does not reach every room, or the equipment is older.
The household added devices, a home office, or a new member.
questions: How many devices are usually connected at the same time in your home?
What do people use the internet for most: streaming, gaming, video calls, or working from home?
Are there rooms where the Wi-Fi is weaker than you'd like?
offers.seed: With everyone online at once in the evenings, you might find a faster plan helps. There's no need to decide anything today, but I'm glad to go over it whenever you like.
offers.bridge: Since you mentioned the video calls freezing when the kids are streaming, can I share an option that's built for busier households like yours?
value: Describe what would feel different for this household, such as smoother video calls while others stream, rather than speed numbers alone.
Avoid promising specific speeds or coverage, because results vary by device and home setup.
disclosure: The new monthly price, any promotional term, and the standard rate afterward
Any equipment change, equipment charge, or installation step
Taxes and fees, and how the change affects the next bill, including partial months

objection.says: My internet is fine the way it is.
objection.acknowledge: That's fair. If it's working for you, there's no reason to change it.
objection.clarify: Just so I understand, do the evening slowdowns you mentioned still bother you, or have they settled down?
objection.respond: If they still come up, the upgrade is mainly about keeping things smooth when everyone is online. If not, your current plan may be the right fit.

offers.note: Resolve technical issues first. Recommend an upgrade only when the household's usage, not a fault, is the reason for the slowdown. Confirm current plans and pricing in approved resources.

offers.title: TV Package Offers
offers.summary: Adding, changing, or right-sizing TV packages and channels, based on what the household actually watches.
fits: The customer asks about a channel, sports, or a program they cannot get.
The customer says they pay for channels they never watch.
Viewing habits have changed, such as a new sports season or more streaming.
The customer has questions about TV boxes in other rooms.
questions: What do you and your household watch most, and on which TVs?
Are there channels or sports you're missing right now?
How much of your viewing happens through streaming apps versus live TV?
offers.seed: If you ever want to make sure your TV package matches what you actually watch, I'm happy to review it with you. Some customers find a better fit that way.
offers.bridge: You mentioned paying for channels you don't watch. Would it help if I looked at whether a different package fits your viewing better?
value: Tie the package to the specific channels, sports, or rooms the customer mentioned.
When a smaller package fits better, recommending it builds trust and is still a relevant offer.
disclosure: The package price, any promotional term, and the standard rate afterward
TV box or equipment charges for each TV
Taxes, fees, and any other monthly charges that apply to TV service
When the change takes effect and how the next bill will look

objection.acknowledge: That makes sense. A lot of households watch mostly through streaming now.
objection.clarify: Is there anything you still watch on live TV, like local channels or sports?
objection.respond: If there is, I can look at whether a package built around those makes sense alongside your streaming. If not, we can leave things as they are.

offers.note: Confirm current packages, equipment, and TV-related charges in approved resources before coaching on TV offers.

offers.title: Retention Offers
offers.summary: Options for a customer who is considering canceling or downgrading, presented through the retention process after understanding the reason.
fits: The customer asks to cancel, downgrade, or remove a service.
The customer mentions a competitor's price or offer.
The bill has become hard to afford.
Repeated service problems have frustrated the customer.
questions: Can you tell me what's prompting you to think about canceling?
If we could address that, would you want to keep your service?
What matters most to you in your service right now: price, reliability, or something else?
offers.seed: Thank you for telling me, and for being with us. Before we go further, I'd like to understand what's behind the decision so I can see what I can do.
offers.bridge: I understand price is the main reason. Let me check which options are available on your account, so you can make the best decision for your household.
value: Address the underlying reason first: fix a service issue, review the bill, or explain options that fit the new budget.
Present only the retention options the process allows, and respect the customer's final decision.
disclosure: What changes on the account and when
The new price, any promotional term, and the rate afterward
Any equipment returns or charges that apply if a service is removed
The customer's confirmed decision and the next steps

objection.acknowledge: I appreciate you being upfront about that, and I understand price matters.
objection.clarify: Is price the main reason, or is there anything else about the service that hasn't worked for you?
objection.respond: Let me check which options are available on your account through our retention process, so you can compare with the full picture before you decide.

offers.note: Confirm the current retention process, which options the agent can present, eligibility, and when another team handles the request.

objectionPrinciple: Acknowledge, clarify, respond. A price concern or a request for time is an invitation to clarify. A clear no is respected the first time, with at most one respectful clarification, and the call closes warmly.

objections.acknowledge: I understand. Keeping the monthly bill manageable matters.
objections.clarify: Is it the monthly price itself, or the change from what you pay now?
objections.respond: Let me make sure you're comparing the full picture, including anything you'd no longer need to pay for elsewhere. If it still doesn't fit your budget, that's completely okay.
objections.close: That's completely fine. Thank you for considering it. Is there anything else I can help you with today?

objections.says: I need to think about it.
objections.acknowledge: That's reasonable. It's a decision worth thinking through.
objections.clarify: Is there a part you're unsure about, such as the price or how it would work for you, that I can clear up while we're on the phone?
objections.respond: If it helps, I can recap the key details so you have them while you think it over.
objections.close: Of course. You can reach out whenever you're ready, and we'll pick it up from there.

objections.says: I'm happy with what I have.
objections.acknowledge: I'm glad it's working well for you.
objections.clarify: Out of curiosity, is there anything you'd change about your current setup if you could?
objections.respond: If something comes to mind, that's where this could help. If not, your current setup may be the right fit.
objections.close: Sounds good. Your service is all set from today's call.

objections.says: I don't want to be locked into anything.
objections.acknowledge: That's a fair concern. Nobody wants surprises later.
objections.clarify: Is it a commitment period you're worried about, or the possibility of the price changing?
objections.respond: Let me check exactly which terms apply to this offer and explain them clearly, so you know what you'd be agreeing to before you decide.
objections.close: Understood. Thank you for hearing me out, and let me know if anything changes.

objections.says: I need to talk it over with someone at home first.
objections.acknowledge: Of course. It makes sense to decide together.
objections.clarify: Is there anything I can explain now that would help when you talk it over?
objections.respond: I can recap the details so you have everything you need for that conversation.
objections.close: That works. Whenever you're both ready, we can go through it again.

objections.says: I don't need anything else right now.
objections.clarify: Can I ask whether anything has changed recently at home, like more people or devices online?
objections.respond: If not, you're all set. If that changes, we can look at options then.
objections.close: You're all set. Thank you for your time today.

objections.says: I've had problems with your service before.
objections.acknowledge: I'm sorry you've had that experience, and I understand why it makes you hesitant.
objections.clarify: Can you tell me what happened, so I can make sure it's addressed?
objections.respond: Let's make sure the issue itself is taken care of first. Once it is, I'm happy to revisit options, but only if they would genuinely help.
objections.close: That's fair. My priority today is making sure the service works the way it should.

objections.acknowledge: No problem at all, and thank you for letting me know.
objections.close: Your service is all set from today's call. Is there anything else I can help you with?
objections.guidance: This is a clear no. Respect it the first time and close warmly, with no further attempt.

signals.example: How much would something like that cost?
signals.next: Happy to go through it. So I quote the right option, how would you mainly use it?

signals.example: Does that come with anything else?
signals.next: Good question. Which part matters most to you, so I can focus on that?

signals.example: My phone contract is up next month.
signals.next: When does it wrap up? That could be a good time to compare your options.

signals.signal: More people or devices at home
signals.example: My son just moved back home.
signals.next: How many devices are usually online at the same time now?

signals.example: My cell phone bill keeps going up.
signals.next: What would you most like to change about your current plan?

signals.example: I'm working from home a few days a week now.
signals.next: How are video calls holding up when others are online?

signals.example: We're moving in a few weeks.
signals.next: Congratulations. Have you set a move date? I can make sure your service is ready at the new address.

signals.example: Is there anything better than what I have?
signals.next: Let's find out. Tell me what you'd want to be better, and I'll look at what fits.
